speaker_role: independent counselor (Eric Dobler, Dobler College Consulting)
commercial_incentive: Yes - closes with an invitation to call the consulting firm for help with financial aid and college search
key_insights: Frames college funding as coming from two main sources: need-based financial aid and merit scholarships
Need-based aid eligibility and amount is determined via FAFSA and, for private colleges, the CSS Profile, based on family income and assets
Merit scholarships are awarded at the time of admission regardless of financial need and can range roughly from $10,000-$15,000 on the low end to $30,000-$40,000+ on the high end
Not all schools offer merit scholarships - many of the most competitive/sought-after schools give little to no merit aid
Advises researching each target school's specific policies on both need-based and merit aid before building a college list, since policies vary significantly by school
specific_numbers_or_facts: Speaker states merit scholarships can range from about $10,000-$15,000 on the low end up to $30,000-$40,000+ on the high end
notable_or_distinctive: Simple, generic two-bucket (need-based vs. merit) framework for financial aid with rough dollar ranges for merit awards; no unique or distinctive insight beyond standard financial aid basics.
reliability_notes: Very short promotional video ending in a direct sales pitch; dollar figures for merit aid are given as rough generalizations without citing specific schools, so they should be treated as ballpark approximations only.
